**Market-implied odds heavily favor a daily maximum of 12–13°C for Wellington on August 2, 2026**, consistent with long-term climatology and current model guidance for early August in the region. Wellington’s winter maxima average around 12°C, driven by the city’s exposure to cool Southern Ocean air masses, frequent westerly winds, and limited solar heating at this latitude during Southern Hemisphere winter. 

NIWA’s June–August 2026 seasonal outlook assigns the highest probability (45%) to near-average temperatures for the Wellington area, with a secondary chance of below-average conditions, reflecting neutral or slightly negative sea-surface temperature anomalies and typical atmospheric circulation patterns. Short-range forecasts from multiple sources, including timeanddate and the UK Met Office, currently project a high near 12°C under mostly sunny or partly cloudy conditions, with light winds that would allow modest daytime warming without strong advection of colder air. 

The modest premium on 13°C in the market likely reflects recent model runs incorporating slightly warmer boundary-layer temperatures or reduced cloud cover compared with pure climatology, while lower-probability outcomes (14°C or above) remain discounted because they would require an atypical warm-sector intrusion or strong high-pressure blocking not currently indicated. Resolution will hinge on the official maximum recorded at Wellington’s primary observing site, with traders closely monitoring any final forecast updates from MetService or NIWA before the 24-hour window closes.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Warsaw Chopin Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pl/warsaw/EPWA.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Typical late-summer conditions feature warm Black Sea and Marmara waters sustaining daytime heating, moderated by variable northerly Etesian winds and patchy cloud development that can trim peak temperatures by 1–2°C. Minor model disagreements on boundary-layer moisture and urban heat retention create the narrow spread, while historical August averages near 28–29°C anchor expectations. Updated high-resolution runs from the Turkish Meteorological Service and 12–18 UTC model cycles in the next 24–48 hours will likely refine these outcomes ahead of market resolution.

Model consensus remains stable, with limited spread in guidance from international and regional agencies, while any strengthening of onshore flow or localized convection could cap peaks near 32°C.
